components.name: ECDSA on STARK curve (Cairo ECDSA builtin)

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-1 capability shipped in the build: the only dependent of sha1 in the lockfile is zip 0.6.6 (legacy encrypted-archive support, PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA1 for WinZip-AES); no first-party call site exists in this repository (grep for SHA-1 use in src/ comes up empty). Same lockfile entry as the LIB-sha1 package object; replaceable only upstream in the zip crate, or by dropping the encrypted-zip feature chain.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Posture-control observation: five non-constant-time digest comparisons in the sequencer-side state/declare paths of the Starknet execution engine. Both operands at every site are public values (on-chain class hashes and a well-known sentinel), so no secret is recoverable through the timing channel — the premise of the rule does not create an exploitable leak here; recorded so a reviewer can see the == comparisons are deliberate cache/state checks, not MAC verifications.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: P-256 (secp256r1) EC point arithmetic exposed to Cairo programs as the secp256r1 curve-builtin syscalls (point decode, add, scalar-mul, get_xy), implemented over the p256 crate in NativeSyscallHandler, plus #[cfg(test)] unit tests (e.g. secp256r1_new at ~1424). Quantum-unsafe under Shor; which curves the Starknet protocol exposes is decided upstream in the Starknet OS spec, not here.

properties.value: p256 crate (RustCrypto) 0.13.2, a direct first-party dependency declared in Cargo.toml. The engine uses its EC point operations for the Starknet OS secp256r1 curve builtin; the ECDSA P-256 primitive it also provides is available in the built artifact but has no first-party sign/verify call site — presence is what the inventory records. Which curves the Starknet OS exposes is protocol-fixed upstream.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: RustCrypto secp256k1 provider, a direct first-party dependency. It powers the secp256k1 curve-builtin syscalls (EC point decode/add/scalar-mul) in the Starknet execution engine; its ECDSA-secp256k1 capability (the ecdsa crate, Cargo.lock:2534) is compiled into the binary with no first-party sign/verify call site. The crate version is changeable here, but the curve is fixed by the Starknet OS builtin specification.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: RustCrypto P-256 (secp256r1) provider, a direct first-party dependency. It powers the secp256r1 curve-builtin syscalls (EC point decode/add/scalar-mul/get_xy) alongside the k256-based secp256k1 builtins; its ECDSA P-256 capability is compiled in with no first-party sign/verify call site. Curve choice is protocol-fixed upstream.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: HMAC capability compiled into the binaries through three transitive paths: the keystore path (eth-keystore via starknet-rs signers — Web3 Secret Storage HMAC-SHA2 authentication of keystore files), the archive path (zip 0.6.6 via cairo-vm — encrypted-zip support), and inside starknet-crypto 0.5.2/0.6.1 for RFC-6979 deterministic ECDSA nonce generation. No first-party HMAC call site exists; parameters are chosen upstream. Not quantum-urgent (Grover-only).
